article_title: Dynamic Learning Solutions: A System for Personalized Educational Video Generation
citation: Siddhanth Sridhar, Shreya Chaurasia, Baddela Sai Yaswantha Reddy, Deepak Parmar, and Dr. Shylaja S S. (2026). Dynamic Learning Solutions: A System for Personalized Educational Video Generation. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14408
title: Multilingual synchronized narration module using Google Text-to-Speech
description: The voiceover component converts script dialogues into audio aligned with video segments. The article states that "Frame looping ensures precise narration-to-visual matching for instructional clarity," and TTS computes speech duration with text segmentation to time audio to specific scenes. It supports multilingual synthesis and translation (e.g., English to Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu) using Google Translate and gTTS to generate MP3 audio compatible across platforms.
requirements: Scene text file from the RAG stage as narration input
Speech-duration computation and text segmentation for scene-level timing
constraints: Synchronization relies on looping scenes to match narration length rather than generating visuals to fit audio
target_learners: multilingual learners, including speakers of Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, and Telugu
target_learning_goals: accessible, narrated multimedia explanations synchronized with visuals
examples: The system supports translation-based generation, e.g., English to Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, producing MP3 audio across platforms
key_sources: Siddhanth Sridhar, Shreya Chaurasia, Baddela Sai Yaswantha Reddy, Deepak Parmar, and Dr. Shylaja S S. (2026). Dynamic Learning Solutions: A System for Personalized Educational Video Generation. arXiv preprint. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14408

article_title: Gynaecology Teaching Associates in Medical Education-A Scoping Review.
citation: Kelly Caitlin, Bell Emily, Brown Megan E. L., Stelling Heidi. (2026). Gynaecology Teaching Associates in Medical Education—A Scoping Review. The Clinical Teacher. https://doi.org/10.1111/tct.70460
title: Four-domain conceptual framework of GTA programmes: educational outcomes at the core, intersecting with ethics, finance, and representation/standardisation, all shaping implementation
description: The review's conceptual framework organises the GTA literature into four interrelated domains: educational outcomes, finance, ethical considerations, and representation and standardisation. Educational outcomes sit at the core, intersecting with the three surrounding domains, while an outer box represents factors directly influencing implementation; ethics and finance extend most explicitly into this implementation space. The framework is presented in Figure 1 and summarised in Table 2, which maps barriers and enablers by factor.
requirements: The framework is a mapping of the existing GTA literature as synthesised inductively from 83 included sources via thematic synthesis.
constraints: As a scoping review, the aim was to map the literature rather than appraise effectiveness, so conclusions about impact should be interpreted cautiously.
target_learners: undergraduate medical students learning pelvic examination
examples: Figure 1 positions educational outcomes at the centre of the GTA literature with ethics, finance and standardisation intersecting it and feeding into implementation factors.
key_sources: Kelly Caitlin, Bell Emily, Brown Megan E. L., Stelling Heidi. (2026). Gynaecology Teaching Associates in Medical Education—A Scoping Review. The Clinical Teacher. https://doi.org/10.1111/tct.70460

article_title: Does Context Matter? Convergent and Divergent Findings in the Cross-Institutional Evaluation of Graduate Teaching Assistant Professional Development Programs.
citation: Reeves Todd D., Hake Laura E., Chen Xinnian, Frederick Jennifer, Rudenga Kristin, Ludlow Larry H., O'Connor Clare M. (2018). Does Context Matter? Convergent and Divergent Findings in the Cross-Institutional Evaluation of Graduate Teaching Assistant Professional Development Programs. CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.17-03-0044
title: Conceptual framework for GTA professional development research and evaluation
description: The article is grounded in a framework (from Reeves et al., 2016) in which "The framework articulates three key PD program outcomes variables: GTA cognition; GTA teaching practice; and undergraduate student outcomes." These outcomes are posited to be linearly and probabilistically related: PD changes GTA cognition, which changes teaching practice, which changes student outcomes. The framework also contains three categories of contextual variables (GTA training design, institutional, and GTA characteristics) and two categories of moderators (implementation variables and GTA characteristics, invoking Dane and Schneider's adherence, exposure, and participant responsiveness concepts). The present study tests the framework's assertion that PD effects vary as a function of contextual factors such as GTA characteristics.
requirements: Multidimensional measurement of GTA cognition, teaching practice, and student outcomes to trace the posited sequential relationships
constraints: The relationships posited are probabilistic rather than wholly deterministic; teacher cognition is not always aligned with practice
target_learners: Graduate teaching assistants in introductory STEM courses
target_learning_goals: Teaching self-efficacy, teaching anxiety, pedagogical knowledge, and instructional practice
examples: The study compared three ST-infused presemester workshop programs at three universities along GTA cognition and student-rating outcome dimensions
key_sources: Reeves Todd D., Hake Laura E., Chen Xinnian, Frederick Jennifer, Rudenga Kristin, Ludlow Larry H., O'Connor Clare M. (2018). Does Context Matter? Convergent and Divergent Findings in the Cross-Institutional Evaluation of Graduate Teaching Assistant Professional Development Programs. CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.17-03-0044
